## Gravity work inside the vertical implicit operator (`implicit-scheme`) {#sec-ch06-vic}

### Summary

The VIC solves each $x_1$ column implicitly for the stage's changes of mass, normal momentum and energy (the
time-integration chapter covers the solve). Gravity enters it twice. The momentum row's mass column and the
energy row's momentum column hold the gravity source Jacobian $\Phi$[^rg-1f2c44c9087e], the linearisation of the body force
$\rho g_1$ and of the cell work $\rho v_1g_1$. With `gravity-work: face` the energy row is changed so that it
books the face form of the mass the solve itself moves; booked after the solve instead, that work makes a tall
column blow up at large implicit steps. Where it sets in depends on the acoustic Courant number and on $N\Delta t$,
with $N$ the buoyancy (Brunt–Väisälä) frequency [s$^{-1}$], so that $N\Delta t$ is the time step in units of the buoyancy period over $2\pi$ (@tbl-ch06-vic-onset); the 45-cell column where it was found blew up at acoustic Courant 65.6.[^ch06-vic-283] With `gravity-work: cell` the energy row adds
only the dissipative part of the face form. After the solve two corrections book the work of the mass that the
solve's projection and its availability clamp moved differently from what the matrix assumed, so the booked
energy matches the mass actually moved.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Puts the gravity work into the vertical implicit correction (VIC), @eq-ch06-vic-rows, so the solve books it.

**Data.** The gravity entries of the energy row (and, through $\Phi$, the momentum row) of each block row.

**Placement.** Once per stage per column, when the VIC rows are assembled; the work corrections after the solve.

**Activation.** `implicit-scheme` 1 or 9 with `const-gravity`; the rows follow `gravity-work`.

**Guarantee / limits.** A linearisation about the stage state; the post-solve corrections match the mass actually moved.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch06-vic-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathbf e_{m_1}$ the unit row vector of the normal-momentum unknown;
$[\mathsf X]_\rho$ and $[\mathsf X]_E$ the mass and energy rows of a block $\mathsf X$; $m_{1,i}=\mathbf e_{m_1}\mathbf q_i$ the
normal momentum of cell $i$ (appendix A $m_1$). $\mathsf A_i$[^rg-47f774f5b4d6], $\mathsf B_i$, $\mathsf C_i$, $\mathsf A^\pm$,
$\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i$[^rg-26618cb146eb], $\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i$ and $\boldsymbol\delta_i$ are defined in @sec-appa. $N$ is the buoyancy (Brunt–Väisälä) frequency of the column [s$^{-1}$], and $N\Delta t$
the dimensionless time step in which @tbl-ch06-vic-onset gives the blow-up onset; the same letter is squared in the
spurious stratification $N^2_{\mathrm{eff}}$ of @sec-ch05-wbref4.

Under `face-wallc` the face work stays outside the operator and is swapped in after the solve, with the wall cells
keeping the cell work; setup warns about it. With the corrected-PE switch on, the energy row also carries part of
that scheme's work (@sec-ch06-dwork).[^ch06-vic-src]

[^ch06-vic-283]: The tall-column blow-up is recorded in chengcli/snapy#283. [source: `sources/gw__GRAVITY_WORK_TECH_REPORT_draft.md`
    §5.2: a balanced isothermal column at rest, 45 cells of 29.9 km, rk3, WENO5[^rg-21ac94b75174], LMARS[^rg-d3152948490d], implicit scheme 9; at
    $\Delta t$ = 997 s (vertical acoustic Courant 65.6) $\max\lvert w\rvert$ grows 2.7 times per step, at
    $\Delta t$ = 100 s (Courant 6.6) it stays at rest. That is one column, not a general threshold.]

[^ch06-vic-src]: The face work in the operator came in with chengcli/snapy#283, the projection and clamp work with
    chengcli/snapy#285.

### Derivation

**The operator this section adds to.** The VIC works on a reduced state per cell, not on $\mathbf U$: the unknown
of block row $i$ is $\mathbf q_i = (\rho, \rho v_1, E)_i$ with `implicit-scheme` 1 and
$(\rho, \rho v_1, \rho v_2, \rho v_3, E)_i$ with 9 (@eq-ch07-vic-size), $v_1$ the $x_1$ velocity and $\rho$ the *total*
density, dry air plus every species; the species ride on it and are redistributed after the solve
(@sec-ch07-vic-redistribute). Each column is one block-tridiagonal system
$\mathsf B_i\boldsymbol\delta_{i-1} + \mathsf A_i\boldsymbol\delta_i + \mathsf C_i\boldsymbol\delta_{i+1} = \mathbf r_i$
for the stage increment $\boldsymbol\delta$ of $\mathbf q$. Its flux part is the Roe linearisation of @sec-ch07-vic-assembly, with the same blocks
$\mathsf A_i$, $\mathsf B_i$, $\mathsf C_i$ and the frozen dissipation matrices $\mathsf A^\pm$ of appendix A, notation group 7;
$[\mathsf A^-]_\rho$ and $[\mathsf A^+]_\rho$ are the mass rows of those two matrices. This section adds only gravity entries: the source Jacobian $\Phi$ and the energy-row work
below. $[\mathsf X]_\rho$ and $[\mathsf X]_E$ are the mass and energy rows of a block $\mathsf X$.

The face form @eq-ch06-dwork-face can be written with the weights
$\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i = \tfrac12A_{i-1/2}(x_{1,i}-x_{1,i-1/2})/V_i$ and
$\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i = \tfrac12A_{i+1/2}(x_{1,i+1/2}-x_{1,i})/V_i$ as
$W^{\mathrm{face}}_i = 2g_1(\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_iF_{i+1/2}+\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_iF_{i-1/2})$. The solve's own
mass flux, linearised, is $F_{i+1/2} = \tfrac12(m_{1,i}+m_{1,i+1}) - \tfrac12[\mathsf A^+]_\rho(\mathbf q_{i+1}-\mathbf q_i)$
with $\mathbf q$ the unknowns and $m_1=\mathbf e_{m_1}\mathbf q$. Substituting, and moving the work to the left-hand
side, the gravity entries of the energy row of block row $i$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}
[\mathsf B_i]_E &= -g_1\,\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i\big(\mathbf e_{m_1} + [\mathsf A^-]_\rho\big),\\
[\mathsf A_i]_E &= -g_1\big(\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i+\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i\big)\mathbf e_{m_1}
  - g_1\big(\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i[\mathsf A^+]_\rho - \omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i[\mathsf A^-]_\rho\big),\\
[\mathsf C_i]_E &= -g_1\,\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i\big(\mathbf e_{m_1} - [\mathsf A^+]_\rho\big).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-vic-rows}

@eq-ch06-vic-rows is assembled in `vic_assemble_full_impl` from `Phi` and the rows under `face_work`
({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}),
with the weights `work_lo` and `work_hi`, built from the grid as `_g_work_lo` and `_g_work_hi`
({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}).
`vicwork_check.py` `[C1]` ports the rows and finds them equal to minus the linearised face work to
$7\times10^{-15}$ over 200 random rows. On a Cartesian column both weights are $\tfrac14$, and the code's Cartesian
branch writes that value in exactly (`[C2]`). With `gravity-work: cell` the momentum entry stays $-g_1$ from
$\Phi$, the cell work, and only the $[\mathsf A^\pm]_\rho$ terms are added (`[C3]`).

After the solve the code books $\phi_i$ times the difference between the raw solved mass change, the explicit
change and the mass the projection moved, and the potential-energy flux of the mass the availability clamp moved
minus what was requested. The first vanishes when the solve is applied as solved; the second keeps
$E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ over a closed column (`[C4]`). `[C21]`–`[C23]` of `derivation_check.py` derive the three
rows of @eq-ch06-vic-rows symbolically from the linearised flux.[^ch06-vic-chk]

[^ch06-vic-chk]: [sha: snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5, ported line for line: the energy rows of
    `vic_assemble_full_impl`,
    `work_lo`/`work_hi` and the projection and clamp work; deck: the check itself; run:
    `python3 src/snapy_report/ch06/checks/vicwork_check.py`, CPU, double, 1 process; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6; output

### Numerical method

@fig-ch06-vic-rows shows the energy-row entries per mode. The rows are assembled once per stage per column, for the
full VIC (`vic_assemble_full`) and the partial VIC (`vic_assemble_partial`) alike, at the stage state, so they
are a linearisation; the step taken is $\Delta t_c$. With `face` the explicit face correction is added to the
right-hand side before the solve, so the energy the solve inverts is the face-form energy, under `face_work_in_operator`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
The column closure at the ends is the VIC's own, reflecting whatever the $x_1$ boundary; immersed solids get no
projection or clamp work. Wall cells use the same rows with the closure applied.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch06-vic-rows
#| fig-cap: "Gravity entries of the energy row of block row i of the VIC, per gravity-work mode: in the blocks of cell i-1 (B), cell i (A) and cell i+1 (C), m is the normal-momentum column and A-, A+ the mass rows of the Roe dissipation matrices at faces i-1/2 and i+1/2; lo and hi are the face-work weights. With cell the momentum entry is the cell work -g; with face it is the face-weighted average of the three cells."
#| fig-alt: "A two-by-three grid of boxes with formulas: rows gravity-work cell and gravity-work face, columns b[i], a[i], c[i]."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch06.figures.fig_vic_rows import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

**A minimal input.**

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `integration`[^rg-ccef979766bf].
```yaml
integration:
  implicit-scheme: 9       # 1 = vic-partial, 9 = vic-full
forcing:
  const-gravity:
    grav1: -9.8            # gravity-work: face, so the face work is in the operator
```

**What the code refuses or warns, and why.**

1. *An `implicit-scheme` other than 0, 1 or 9* is refused ("Unsupported implicit scheme"): there are only two solvers
   ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::type >}}).
2. *A face form whose work is not in the operator* (`face-wallc`) is warned about at setup
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}). The message says that "a tall column at acoustic Courant ~66
   blows up" when the face work sits outside the linearised operator. That number is the 45-cell column where the
   problem was found; in general the onset depends on the Courant number and on $N\Delta t$ (@tbl-ch06-vic-onset).

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch06-vic-rows**
({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}), the general branch:

```cpp
T lower = work_lo[i * stride2], upper = work_hi[i * stride2];           // omega_lo, omega_hi
a[i].row(IPR) -= grav * (upper * Ap.row(IDN) - lower * Am.row(IDN));    // -g1 (w_hi [A+]_rho - w_lo [A-]_rho)
b[i].row(IPR) -= grav * lower * Am.row(IDN);                            // -g1 w_lo [A-]_rho
c[i].row(IPR) += grav * upper * Ap.row(IDN);                            // +g1 w_hi [A+]_rho
if (face_work) {
  a[i](IPR, IVX + dir) += grav * (1. - lower - upper);   // with Phi's cell-work entry: -g1 (w_lo + w_hi) e_m
  b[i](IPR, IVX + dir) -= grav * lower;                  // -g1 w_lo e_m
  c[i](IPR, IVX + dir) -= grav * upper;                  // -g1 w_hi e_m
}
```

The Cartesian branch writes $\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}=\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}=\tfrac14$ in directly (`[C2]` of `vicwork_check.py`).
The sign of the momentum entry is as written: `Phi(IPR, IVX + dir) = grav`, `Phi`
([`vic_assemble_full_impl.h:40`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h#L40)),
`a[i]` subtracts `Phi`
([`:94-96`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h#L94-L96)),
and the face branch adds $g_1(1-\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i-\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i)$ with the weights `lower`
([`:116`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h#L116)),
so the entry is $-g_1+g_1(1-\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i-\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i)=-g_1(\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i+\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i)$, the
$\mathbf e_{m_1}$ coefficient of $[\mathsf A_i]_E$ in @eq-ch06-vic-rows. The rows are also checked by `[C1]` and
`[C21]`–`[C23]`.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| gravity source Jacobian | {{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}} | `Phi` | `const-gravity` |
| energy-row gravity work | {{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}} | `face_work` | `gravity-work` |
| same, partial VIC | {{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_partial_impl.h vic_assemble_partial_impl >}} | `face_work` | `implicit-scheme` |
| weights and mode flags | {{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}} | `kVicFaceWork` | `gravity-work` |
| projection and clamp work | {{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}} | `projection_work` | |
| face-wallc swap | {{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}} | `swap` | `face-wallc` |
| face work in the operator | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::face_work_in_operator >}} | `face_work_in_operator` | `gravity-work` |

: Code map of the gravity work in the implicit operator. {#tbl-ch06-vic-code}

1. Form the face weights as `_g_work_lo` and `_g_work_hi`, once per grid, and keep them ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}).
2. Choose the mode flags from `face_work_in_operator` and `gravity_work` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}).
3. In `vic_assemble_full_impl`, add the Cartesian or general rows under `face_work` ({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}).
4. Add the explicit face correction before the solve, as `gravity_energy_correction` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
5. After the solve, add `projection_work` and `clamp_work` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}).
6. For `face-wallc`, swap in the face work after the solve as `swap` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_implicit_face_work_operator_python` | rest column at rest, Courant 66-657 | $10^{-7}$ m s$^{-1}$ | `W_TOL` |
| `test_implicit_face_work_operator_python` | $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ drift | $10^{-11}$ rel. | `EPE_TOL` |
| `test_implicit_face_work_operator_python` | with `implicit-scheme` 9, rk3s4 converges no slower than rk3 | none: a comparison of the two fitted rates against a Courant-1/32 rk3 reference | the assertion itself (@sec-ch07-vic-stage) |
| `test_implicit_stratified_solid_python` | clamp energy, solids | $10^{-11}$ rel. | `EPE_TOL` |
| `test_forcing.release` | energy under rk3 stage weights | $10^{-9}$ abs. | test threshold |

: Tests of the gravity work in the implicit operator; assertions read from the test sources at the pin, not run.
{#tbl-ch06-vic-tests}

`[C1]` of `vicwork_check.py` finds the ported rows equal to minus the linearised face work to $7\times10^{-15}$ over
200 random rows; `[C2]` the Cartesian weights $\tfrac14$; `[C3]` the cell-mode rows; `[C4]` the clamp work keeping
$E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ over a closed column.

`test_implicit_face_work_operator` puts the tall column of the blow-up above into discrete balance and runs it with
`gravity-work: face`, full and partial VIC, at acoustic Courant 65.6, 197 and 657, requiring `W_TOL` and `EPE_TOL`
(module constants of {{< code tests/test_implicit_face_work_operator.py >}}). At the pin the same `main` also runs
a third assertion, with no tolerance constant: it fits the $w$ error of rk3 and of rk3s4 against an
rk3 run at Courant $1/32$ and fails if rk3s4's rate is the lower of the two (@sec-ch07-vic-stage has the rk3s4
weights and the measured orders). The plain arms run with
`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0`; the `_radial_exact_python` entries run the same scripts with it on and measure
$E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$. `implicit_gravity_work_holds_under_rk3_stage_weighting` also has a CUDA case. Measured values at the pin are
**missing evidence**.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
`face-wallc` with an implicit scheme books the face work after the solve, and a tall column then blows up. The onset
depends on the acoustic Courant number and on $N\Delta t$, the time step in units of the buoyancy period over $2\pi$
(@tbl-ch06-vic-onset); acoustic Courant about 66 is the
onset of the one 45-cell column it was found on, not a general threshold.
:::

| acoustic Courant number | $N\Delta t$ at onset |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2.3 to 2.9 |
| 10 | about 7 |
| 100 | about 20 |

: Onset of the after-solve (`face-wallc`) blow-up of a tall column under an implicit scheme, from a linear model of
the column.[^ch06-vic-onset] $N\Delta t$ is the time step in units of the buoyancy period over $2\pi$, with $N$ the buoyancy (Brunt–Väisälä)
frequency of the column. The
table is to be extended from the archived onset table, which covers acoustic Courant 1 to 200. {#tbl-ch06-vic-onset}

[^ch06-vic-onset]: [source: linear-model result in the project discussion thread 1794212148.557499, archived there as a
    bundle whose onsets for acoustic Courant 1 to 200 are a CSV, sha256 `3a959ec3…8d7e7a` (abbreviated as recorded in
    the thread; the full digest is not given there). The bundle is not in the repository, and no deck, script, sha or
    command for it is recorded here, so the three rows are **missing evidence** until that CSV and the model that
    produced it are committed with their run record; the table is to be extended from it.]

- The rows are a linearisation about the stage state.
- The VIC closes each column as a reflecting wall whatever the $x_1$ boundary (time-integration chapter).
- Combinations with the study switches: @sec-ch12-matrix.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-1f2c44c9087e]: $\Phi$ — the gravity source Jacobian; upright, not sans-serif like the other matrices, because the math font has no sans-serif Greek and `\mathsf` drops the glyph in the PDF

[^rg-47f774f5b4d6]: $\mathsf A_i, \mathsf B_i, \mathsf C_i$ — the diagonal, lower and upper blocks of row $i$ of the block-tridiagonal system

[^rg-26618cb146eb]: $\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i, \omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i$ — the implicit face-work weights $\tfrac12A_{i\mp1/2}\lvert x_{1,i}-x_{1,i\mp1/2}\rvert/V_i$

[^rg-21ac94b75174]: WENO5 — fifth-order weighted essentially non-oscillatory reconstruction

[^rg-d3152948490d]: LMARS — low-Mach approximate Riemann solver

[^rg-ccef979766bf]: integration — time-integration options
